title: Orchestrated cross-region failover & traffic-shift runbook for hosted + dedicated
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a validated, tested runbook and automation for cross-region outages and controlled traffic shifting that covers both Redwood Hosted API and Dedicated capacity customers. This ticket consolidates learnings from the Mar 2026 cross-region incident, implements immediate bugfixes and durable mitigations, and codifies playbooks for operators to safely route traffic between regions (including model-variant fallbacks and cache-warmup strategies).
incident_summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed correlated p95 latency spikes and request errors originating in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 across both hosted and dedicated deployments. Primary cause was a kernel selection regression combined with KV cache eviction behavior after autoscaler churn on dedicated GPU pools. Impact: degraded responses for ~40% of hosted requests to affected regions and reduced throughput for 3 dedicated customers. Several customers escalated to SEs and SREs during the incident.
mitigation_actions: 2026-03-08 03:12 UTC: Eng oncall forced smart-routing policy to prefer eu-central-1 for affected routes (manual override) to reduce p95 latency
2026-03-08 03:25 UTC: Increased dedicated pool capacity (reserve burst nodes) for two impacted customers to prevent ongoing OOMs
2026-03-08 03:40 UTC: Rolled back the recent kernel optimization flag on runtime nodes in us-west-2 (reverted build r-infer-1.18.3) which stopped new OOM patterns
2026-03-08 04:05 UTC: Warmed KV caches in the target region by replaying recent popular prefixes via the cache-warm endpoint and a targeted batch job
2026-03-08 04:30 UTC: Updated customer-facing status page and proactive SE outreach for top 10 affected customers
proposed_runbook: Phase 0 - Detection: Confirm cross-region scope using global latency dashboard, p95/p99 error heatmap, and dedicated pool telemetry (GPU OOMs, scheduling failures). Use tag 'cross-region' in the incident room.
Phase 1 - Containment: If two or more regions show sustained p95 > 2x baseline AND error rate increase > 3x, initiate cross-region failover protocol.

Phase 2 - Traffic Shift Preparation: Verify capacity in candidate target region (available GPU slots, model variant compatibility, matching quantization profiles). Check KV cache hit rate history and plan for warmup time (estimate warmup RTT per prefix).
1) Enter maintenance window in Console for affected routes and pause background billing-heavy tasks for dedicated customers as needed.
2) Adjust Smart Routing weights: set primary region weight to 0.1 and target region to 0.9 in increments (0 -> 10% -> 50% -> 90%) with 2 minute observation between steps.
3) If using DNS-based mitigation, ensure global LB TTL <= 60s before initiating. Prefer global LB weight updates over DNS for lower lead time.
4) Warm KV caches via /internal/cache-warm for top 200 prefixes and run a controlled synthetic load at 5-10% of production RPS to pre-fill caches.
5) Validate functional correctness: run smoke tests (generation, chat, embeddings) against target region and compare outputs against golden prompts (allowing model-variant deltas).

Phase 4 - Post-shift Validation: Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and client-side observed timeouts for 30 minutes at steady traffic. Ensure SLOs return to acceptable thresholds. If regression observed, revert weights by 50% or fall back to canary route.
Phase 5 - Rollback Criteria: Define automatic rollback triggers: sustained >15% error rate increase, p99 > 3x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes, or CPU/GPU OOMs on >3 nodes in the target region.
Phase 6 - Communication: Standardized templates for status page, customer emails, and internal incident notes. Include expected ETA for final switchover or rollback and list of affected deployments.

Automations to implement: 'rctl shift-traffic --from us-west-2 --to eu-central-1 --percent 50 --step 10 --wait 120s' with dry-run mode and automated pre-checks. Add a 'dry-fallback' flag to immediately rehydrate previous routing on failure triggers.
